extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Euclidean geometry (geometers, mathematicians, classical-geometry learners)
extracted.subtask_description: Classical Euclidean construction propositions: given certain magnitudes, angles, ratios, or positions (parallelograms, squares, circles, segments), determine (construct) lines, points, or rectangles and show they are 'given' in magnitude/position. Each proposition gives conditions and a construction (analysis and composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: IF two straight lines contain a parallelogram given in magnitude, in a given angle; if the excess of the square of the greater above the square of the lesser be given, each of the straight lines shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two straight lines AB, BC that contain a parallelogram AC of given magnitude in a given angle ABC, and given the excess of the square of the greater (BC) above the square of the lesser (BA), then AB and BC are each determined (given) in magnitude and position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis: represent the given excess as a rectangle CB·BD, subtract from square(BC) to get rectangle BC·CD equal to square(AB), use given angle to relate rectangle AB·BC to parallelogram AC, deduce ratios of DB to BA and of BC to BD, hence determine BC and BA. Composition: construct auxiliary given angle and rectangles equal to the given parallelogram and excess, use mean proportion and proportional constructions (bisecting, doubling, joining) to produce AB and BC and complete the parallelogram AC, verifying equalities of rectangles and squares as in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF two straight lines contain a parallelogram given in magnitude, in a given angle; if the sum of the squares of its sides be given, the sides shall each of them be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: If AB and BC contain a given parallelogram ABCD in a given angle ABC, and the sum of the squares of AB and BC is given, then AB and BC are each determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case split: if ABC is right-angled, relate twice the rectangle of two equal lines to sum of squares to decide a square construction; otherwise construct a rectangle equal to the given parallelogram, use semicircle on AC as diameter and place AF at right angles so that a point B on the circumferences yields AB, BC with required rectangle and squares. For non-right angle, use ratio of rectangle AB·BC to AC (given) and reduce to the right-angled construction; composition step-by-step constructs AC, BE, circle, perpendiculars, and finds points giving AB and BC.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF two straight lines contain a given parallelogram in a given angle, and if the excess of the square of one of them above a given space, has a given ratio to the square of the other; each of the straight lines shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two lines AB, BC containing a given parallelogram AC in angle ABC, and given that (square(BC) − given_space) has a given ratio to square(AB), then AB and BC are each determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace the 'given space' by a rectangle CB·BD; subtract it from square(BC) yielding rectangle BC·CD which has a given ratio to square(AB). Construct BF such that square(BF)=BC·CD; using given angles and ratios obtain FB, BC as in Prop. 87 and then scale FB to BA to give AB, BC. Composition: choose auxiliary given angle and rectangles matching given data, apply previous (Prop. 87) to find BC,BF, then make proportional construction to produce BA and complete parallelogram AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF two straight lines contain a given parallelogram in a given angle, and if the square of one of them together with the space which has a given ratio to the square of the other be given, each of the straight lines shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given AB, BC contain parallelogram AC in given angle ABC; if square(BC) together with a space having a given ratio to square(AB) is given, then AB and BC are each determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let square(BD) be the space with given ratio to square(AB); then square(BC)+square(BD) is given. From A draw perpendicular to BC; triangles give ratios so rectangle DB·BC becomes known; with sum of squares and rectangle known, apply Prop. 88 (sum+rectangle case) to determine DB and BC, hence BA; composition uses an auxiliary angle and rectangles to construct DB, BC with required sum and ratio, then build parallelogram AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line drawn within a circle given in magnitude cuts off a segment which contains a given angle; the straight line is given in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.description: In a given circle ABC (given in magnitude), if chord AC cuts off a segment AEC containing a given angle AEC, then the straight line AC (the chord) is determined in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take D center; join AD and extend to E, join EC. Because angle ACE is right and angle AEC is given, triangle ACE is given in species; the ratio EA:AC is determined and since EA (a chord/segment from given circle) is given in magnitude, AC is determined. Construction: use center and right-angle properties to relate known angle to chord length.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line given in magnitude be drawn within a circle given in magnitude, it shall cut off a segment containing a given angle.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a circle ABC and a straight line AC of given magnitude drawn within it, the chord AC will cut off a segment AEC whose contained angle AEC is determined (given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take D center, join AD and extend to E, join EC; EA and AC are given so their ratio is given and because ACE is right, triangle ACE is given in species, hence angle AEC is determined. The construction is direct via center and perpendicularity producing the segment angle from given chord length.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF from any point in the circumference of a circle given in position two straight lines be drawn meeting the circumference and containing a given angle; if the point in which one of them meets the circumference again be given, the point in which the other meets it is also given.
rubrics_metrics.description: From point A on a given circle (given in position), draw AB and AC making given angle BAC; if B is known, then C is determined (given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take D the center and join BD, DC. Since B and D known, BD is given in position; angle BDC is determined by given inscribed angle, so drawing DC from D in given angle meets given circumference again at a unique point C. Construction: use center D and angle BDC to locate C on the given circumference.

rubrics_metrics.name: If from a given point a straight line be drawn touching a circle given in position; the straight line is given in position and magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given point A and circle BC (given in position), the tangent AB from A to the circle is determined in position and magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take D the centre, join DA; DA is given, and DBA is a right angle, so DA is a diameter of the circumcircle of triangle DBA; that circumcircle is determined, intersection with given circle gives B. Thus the tangent AB is located; construction uses center and right-angle/tangent properties to determine AB.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line be drawn from a given point without a circle given in position; the rectangle contained by the segments betwixt the point and the circumference of the circle is given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a point A outside a circle BCD (given in position), and line ABC meeting the circle at B and C, the rectangle BA·AC is determined (given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw AD tangent from A; AD is given in position and magnitude, its square equals BA·AC, so the rectangle BA·AC is given. Construction uses tangent length squared equals product of external and total segments (power of a point).

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line be drawn through a given point within a circle given in position, the rectangle contained by the segments betwixt the point and the circumference of the circle is given.
rubrics_metrics.description: For a given point A inside a given circle BCE, a line BAG meeting circle at B and C has BA·AC determined (given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take D center, extend AD to meet circumference at E,F which are given; EA and AF are each given, so rectangle EA·AF is given and equals BA·AC. This is again the chord-segment product (power of a point). Construction uses center and diametrically opposite intersections to compute product.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line be drawn within a circle given in magnitude cutting off a segment containing a given angle; if the angle in the segment be bisected by a straight line produced till it meets the circumference, the straight lines which contain the given angle shall both of them together have a given ratio to the straight line which bisects the angle: and the rectangle contained by both these lines together which contain the given angle, and the part of the bisecting line cut off below the base of the segment, shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: In a circle given in magnitude, let BC cut off a segment containing given angle BAC; if AD bisects that angle to meet circumference at D, then (BA + AC) : AD is a given ratio, and the rectangle (BA+AC)·(segment ED from AD below BC) is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since BC and BD (or AD) are deduced from the segment chord data (BC drawn cuts off given segment), BD is known; use angle bisector proportionality and similar triangles (relating BA, AC, AG, GE, AD, DB) to obtain the ratio of BA+AC to AD. Also derive equality of rectangle (BA+AC)·DE to known rectangle CB·BD. Construction: join BD, apply angle bisector and similar-triangle relations, or use alternative symmetry construction (extend CA, reflect AB) as given to find the required ratio and rectangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF a straight line be drawn within a circle given in magnitude, cutting off a segment containing a given angle: if the angle adjacent to the angle in the segment be bisected by a straight line produced till it meets the circumference again and the base of the segment; the excess of the straight lines which contain the given angle shall have a given ratio to the segment of the bisecting line which is within the circle; and the rectangle contained by the same excess and the segment of the bisecting line betwixt the base produced and the point where it again meets the circumference, shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given circle and chord BC cutting off segment with given angle BAC; bisect adjacent angle CAF by DAE meeting circumference at D and base produced at E. Then (BA − AC) (the excess GC) has a given ratio to AD, and rectangle (BA − AC)·DE is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct BG parallel to DE meeting AC produced so GC equals BA−AC. Use equal-angle and inscribed-angle equalities to show triangles BGC and BDA are equiangular, giving GC:CB = AD:DB, hence (BA−AC):AD is determined. Show rectangle GC·DE equals CB·BD (given), so the required rectangle is given. Construction uses parallels and similar triangles to convert the bisector data into a proportional statement and a rectangle equal to a readily computed rectangle from known chord segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF from a given point in the diameter of a circle given in position, or in the diameter produced, a straight line be drawn to any point in the circumference, and from that point a straight line be drawn at right angles to the first, and from the point in which this meets the circumference again, a straight line be drawn parallel to the first; the point in which this parallel meets the diameter is given; and the rectangle contained by the two parallels is given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given circle ABC (given in position) and point D on diameter BC (or produced), draw DA to point A on circumference, from A draw AE ⟂ DA meeting circumference at E, then draw EF ∥ DA meeting BC at F. Then F is determined and rectangle AD·EF is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend EF to meet circumference at G and join AG. AG is a diameter, BC is a diameter, so their intersection H (center) is given. From DH (known) and parallelism (AD ∥ FG) deduce HF given; hence F located. Use the fact that chord-parallel properties and symmetry give EF·FG (or AD·EF) equal to the rectangle determined by known segments (power-of-a-point style); conclude AD·EF is given. Construction uses center location and perpendicular/parallel relations to compute the parallel intersection and rectangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: IF from a given point in a straight line given in position, a straight line be drawn to any point in the circumference of a circle given in position; and from this point a straight line be drawn making with the first an angle equal to the difference of a right angle and the angle contained by the straight line given in position, and the straight line which joins the given point and the centre of the circle; and from the point in which the second line meets the circumference again, a third straight line be drawn making with the second an angle equal to that which the first makes with the second: the point in which this third line meets the straight line given in position is given; as also the rectangle contained by the first straight line and the segment of the third betwixt the circumference and the straight line given in position, is given.
rubrics_metrics.description: Given straight line AB (given in position), point C on AB, and circle DEF (given in position) with center G: draw CD to circumference at D; from D draw DF making angle CDF equal to (right angle − angle BCG), let FE be drawn from F making angle DFE equal to CDF, meeting AB at H. Then H is determined and rectangle CD·FH is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses center G, angle manipulations (difference from right angle), and chaining equal-angle constructions so that successive chords/lines meet AB at a computable point H. The rectangle CD·FH is determined by the constructed intersections and equal-angle relations; build successive lines with the specified angular constraints and compute the required segment and rectangle from the intersections.
